newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister won't spare accused politicians.
newsitem.headline: French minister won't spare accused politicians.

text.p: France's new Socialist Justice Minister Elisabeth Guigou said on Thursday she agreed with moves to ban photos of handcuffed suspects before they are charged but questioned whether implicated politicians should be spared.

"I think it is normal one should want to ban photos of handcuffed people appearing in the press or on television before they are charged because that can mark the life of a person who is not necessarily guilty," Guigou told TF1 television.

"But I really wonder about banning all mention of people implicated in a case, specifically public figures. If you hold elected office and are a public personality you have to shoulder some responsibility."
Guigou was commenting on recommendations drawn up by magistrates on the instructions of France's previous centre-right government, presented on Thursday to President Jacques Chirac.

They call for more protection for the presumption of innocence but left-wingers had said when the report was commissioned they suspected it was aimed at protecting rightist politicians, of whom several were then deeply involved in suspected corruption cases.

The report was also said to be aimed at severing controversial links between politicians and state prosecutors, but it fell short of expectations it would urge greater independence for prosecutors who control judges investigating political corruption. Some judges have been held back in the past by government interference.
Guigou said she agreed prosecutors should be free but said she would put pressure on those of them who failed to act against racist insults, revisionist literature or dangerous sects.
Chirac said when the report was handed to him he hoped Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's new cabinet would try to pass its recommendations through parliament.
